transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi. Well, I came in because I'm having some issues at work. I'm a cashier, and lately at the register, I keep getting stuck doing things that just don't really fit the moment. 

Like, I'll start tapping the scanner in a specific pattern, or I'll just... freeze, with my hand hovering right over the cash drawer while a customer is standing there waiting for me. It's causing problems. Last week it actually got me written up by my manager, so I figured I needed to come in and talk to someone about it.
Do you find yourself doing these repetitive patterns, like tapping in a specific pattern, when you're not at work?

Not really, no. I... I haven't noticed it happening at home or anywhere else. It seems to mostly just be when I'm at the register. Like, I don't find myself tapping the counter in my kitchen or freezing up when I'm just going about my own day. It's really just been an issue at work.
Do you feel anxious or uneasy in social situations outside of your job?

No, not really. I mean, I don't go out a whole lot, but when I do... like if I'm at the grocery store or talking to a neighbor, I feel fine. I don't get nervous or anything like that. It's just normal.
Do you feel like you have to tap the scanner in that specific pattern or complete some other action in a certain way when you're at the register?

No, I wouldn't say I feel like I *have* to do it. It's not like an urge or a rule in my head or anything. It's more like... my body just does it. I'll just realize I'm tapping it, or I'll realize I've been standing there frozen. I don't feel anxious if I don't do it, I just... find myself doing it anyway.
Do you feel like these behaviors or episodes at the register are affecting other areas of your life outside of work?

Well, yeah, I'd say they are. I mean, at the store, I'm actually on a formal warning now because of what's been happening. And then outside of my shifts... I don't know, it just takes a toll. I've basically stopped keeping up with my friends. I used to have kayaking plans, but I dropped those, and I don't even return family calls the way I used to. So, yeah, it's definitely affecting things.
Do you feel distressed or upset by these episodes of tapping or freezing when they happen?

No, not really. I mean, I don't get upset or stressed out about it when it's happening. It's just... it's just something that happens. I'm more worried about losing my job over it, honestly, but the actual tapping or standing there? No, it doesn't bother me emotionally.
Did you have any developmental delays as a child, such as delays in walking or talking?
No, not that I know of. My parents never mentioned anything like that to me. As far as I know, I walked and talked around the normal time. Everything was pretty typical back then.
Do you have any thoughts that keep repeating in your mind and are difficult to get rid of?
No, I don't think so. I mean, my mind can get a bit cluttered sometimes, but I wouldn't say I have any thoughts that just repeat over and over or get stuck. It's not like that.
Have you ever had problems with being overwhelmed by certain sights, sounds, or textures?

No, I wouldn't say so. I don't really get overwhelmed by things like that. Sights and sounds are just... normal, I guess. I've never had any issues with textures either. Everything seems pretty standard to me in that regard.
Do you have any strong interests that you feel are unusual or that take up a lot of your time?

No, not really. I don't have any hobbies or interests like that. I mean, I just go to work, do my shifts at the store, and when I get home I just kind of relax. There's nothing unusual that I spend all my time on.
Do you have difficulty making friends or connecting with people outside of work?

No, I wouldn't say I have difficulty. I mean, I don't really have a lot of friends, but it's not because I can't make them. I just... I mostly keep to myself. After work, I prefer to just be at home. I talk to people enough at the store, so I don't really feel the need to go out of my way to connect with people outside of that. It's just how I like it.
Have you ever had any behaviors or interests that you felt compelled to repeat over and over, outside of the tapping or freezing at work?

No, I don't think so. I mean, besides what happens at the store... no. There's nothing else I feel compelled to repeat. When I'm at home, I just kind of go about my evening normally. I don't have any habits or routines that I feel stuck on doing over and over again.
Do you have any rituals or routines that you follow every day?

No, not really. I mean, I get up, I go to work, I come home... eat dinner, maybe watch some TV. But I wouldn't call it a ritual. It's just... just a normal day. I don't have anything I *have* to do in a certain way or anything like that.
Did you have any strong, highly focused interests as a child?

No, I don't think so. I was pretty much just a regular kid. I liked the usual things, played outside... but I never had one specific thing I was obsessed with or anything like that. Just normal kid stuff, really.
Did you ever feel like you had to follow certain rules or routines in your daily life as a child?

No, I don't remember anything like that. I mean, just the normal rules my parents set, you know, like doing chores or getting homework done. But I never had my own routines that I felt forced to follow. I was pretty easygoing about that kind of stuff, just took things day by day.
Did you ever feel like you had a strong attachment to certain objects as a child?

No, not that I can remember. I mean, I had toys I liked playing with, sure, but I didn't have anything I carried around with me everywhere. No special blanket or... or a favorite toy I couldn't be without, nothing like that. When I was done playing with something, I just put it away. I just kind of played with whatever was there.
Do you find it difficult to be flexible with changes in your daily routine?

No, not really. I mean, my schedule as a cashier changes from week to week anyway, so... I'm pretty used to things shifting around. If something comes up or my routine changes, it doesn't really bother me. I just adjust and go with it.
Did you ever have periods where you felt a strong need to organize things in a very specific way?

No, I haven't. I mean, I keep my place tidy enough, but I don't get hung up on putting things in an exact order or anything like that. I just put things away where they fit. I've never really felt any kind of strong urge to organize stuff in a specific way.
Do you have any behaviors or activities that you enjoy doing in your free time that you find yourself thinking about or wanting to do even when you're not doing them?

No, I don't think so. I mean, I have things I do to pass the time when I'm not at work, like watching TV or maybe reading, but I don't really fixate on them. When I'm at the store ringing people up, I'm just focused on my job. I don't really find myself daydreaming about getting back to a hobby or... or feeling like I need to be doing a specific activity. It's just stuff to do when I happen to have free time, that's all.
Have you ever had difficulty understanding sarcasm or nuances in other people's language?

No, I don't think so. I usually catch on just fine if someone is joking or being sarcastic. You get a lot of different personalities coming through my line at the store, and I've never really had any trouble picking up on what they mean. I've never had anyone tell me I missed the joke or didn't understand them, anyway. So, no, I'd say I understand people's meaning pretty clearly.
